newsitem.title: UK: BA makes offer to end ground staff dispute.
newsitem.headline: BA makes offer to end ground staff dispute.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday it had submitted a package of proposals to ground staff to try to settle a dispute over the planned sale of its Heathrow longhaul catering unit.
BA, which is also in arbitrated talks on a separate dispute over pay and conditions for cabin crew, said ground staff were now considering the offer which was made after 48 hours of talks.
BA is planning to sell off its Heathrow longhaul catering unit as part of a plan to save one billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by the end of the century and outsource non-core operations.
The airline believes it is better served by outside operators, who currently deliver around 85,000 of the 110,000 meals delivered daily to the British carrier.
But union representatives are fighting the sell-off, worried that workers will suffer pay cuts and lose valuable perks. They have threatened possible strike action.
BA said its proposals secured terms and conditions for employees under a new owner of the catering business.

It said the package included a three-year period to apply for other jobs in British Airways, a three-year period to apply for early retirement or voluntary severance and no compulsory redundancies for at least three years with current pay levels protected.
The airline said it would also protect staff travel privileges, holiday pay and other entitlements.
